messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Service inference-grpc in az1a crossing error-rate threshold (5xx) and p95 latency target. Auto-ticket created.

kayla.sre: seeing it in graphs — p95 jumped to ~1.2s, 5xx ~6% on az1a-only pools. Hosts show high retransmits on tcp.

kayla.sre: quick check: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide` shows node affinity pinned to az1a for this deployment (recent autoscale bump).

mike.infra: starting network checks on az1a. doing traceroutes from lb to nodes and tcpdump on problem host.

anika.runtime: log tail from runtime proxy: `grpc: connection error: remote error: connection reset by peer` repeated, also high conn queue lengths.

mike.infra: `ss -s` on node1 shows many orphaned SYN_RECV and retransmit counts high. suspect AWS network plane flaps.

chris.prod: customers report elevated tail latency and sporadic 502s. No broad region outage, only az1a. A few customers hitting rate-limits after retries.

kayla.sre: immediate mitigations: 1) shift traffic away from az1a pools for affected models; 2) spin warm nodes in az1b; 3) reduce per-node max connections to avoid head-of-line. Applying policy now.

mike.infra: executing reroute via gateway policy: `redwoodctl route modify --service inference-grpc --avoid-az az1a --weight az1b:1.0`

anika.runtime: temporarily lowering keepalive interval and enabling connection drain on az1a hosts. `runtimectl drain --env inference --az az1a --grace 30s`

support-bot: Notifying affected customer workspaces: workspace-137, startup-x, partner-ops. Template message queued.

kayla.sre: monitoring: error-rate trending down after reroute, p95 dropping towards normal. Still seeing packet drops on low-level metrics for az1a.

mike.infra: AWS checks: ENI metrics show rx_err/rx_drop spike on several instances in az1a. Opening AWS support case (case# 2026-RED-2201).

chris.prod: Customer impact — transient failures and retries for ~15% of requests routed initially to az1a; majority retried successfully but some timeouts observed. Logging L3 for SLA assessment.

kayla.sre: plan: keep az1a avoided for capacity scheduling, continue draining problematic hosts, and scale up az1b warm pool to absorb traffic. If AWS restores NIC health, we'll gradually reintroduce via canary.

mike.infra: placed a soft limit on new task placement in az1a (`scheduler: avoid az1a`), and kicked rolling update to replace suspect instances with fresh AMIs that include net driver tuning.

anika.runtime: runtime config change rolled: reduced max inflight per-worker from 256 -> 120 and enabled backpressure to grpc gateway. Should reduce queue blowups.

kayla.sre: summary for handoff -> oncall-rotations: az1a experiencing NIC-level packet drops causing TCP retransmits, grpc connection resets, and tail latency/5xx for inference pools. Major mitigation enacted: traffic routed away, draining hosts, scaling neighbor AZ, AWS case opened. Customer impact limited but measurable.

oncall-rotations: acknowledged. taking over monitoring for next 8h. list of checks saved to incident ticket.

support-bot: Updated status page: we are investigating increased errors affecting inference in a single AZ; mitigation in progress.

kayla.sre: any follow-ups before I sign off?

mike.infra: will keep AWS case updates in the ticket and post when ENI metrics stabilize. recommend postmortem to cover scheduler AZ affinity rules and warm pool placement logic.

anika.runtime: I'll prepare a short runbook tweak to adjust max connections and backpressure defaults to prevent recoverable flaps from cascading.

kayla.sre: handing to oncall-rotations. tagging SLO/ops to review customer impact. signing off — kayla

oncall-rotations: taking, will notify if we need paging escalation. :thumbsup:
